plan: The plan will install loft insulation, then cavity wall insulation (needs checking on site first), then a smart thermostat (needs checking on site first), and finally solar panels. The order is chosen because solar panels are applied last as they only reduce the electricity bought from the grid.
energy: Gas use is estimated to {energy_results.change.gas_saving_kwh|change}. Grid electricity use is estimated to {energy_results.change.grid_elec_saving_kwh|change}. Overall, the energy the home buys is estimated to {energy_results.change.purchased_saving_kwh|change}. Each measure’s saving is already worked out on the energy left after the previous measures, so the figures reflect their interaction.
cost: The estimated cost of the selected measures is {cost_results.package_cost_gbp}. Changes to energy bills are not estimated because {cost_results.bill_reason}.
value: An indicative property‑value range is not estimated because {valuation.reason}.
not_suitable: Double glazing is not suitable because windows are already double glazed. Cavity wall insulation needs checking first because wall type, rating or age is not recorded. A smart thermostat needs checking first because heating controls are not recorded.
caveats: The savings for a smart thermostat use typical published ranges, not measured UK data. Cavity wall insulation is applied conditionally: verify walls rating, wall type. Smart thermostat is applied conditionally: verify controls. Combined insulation and controls savings may be overestimated: in national measured data, real combined savings were lower.
